questions.question: Under the Regulating Act of $1773$, which specific structural change was made regarding the administration of the Bombay and Madras presidencies?

answerOptions.text: The Governors of Bombay and Madras were granted independent legislative powers for their respective territories.
answerOptions.rationale: This act actually began the process of centralization by reducing the independence of these presidencies.

answerOptions.text: The presidencies were made subordinate to the Governor-General of Bengal.
answerOptions.rationale: This was a foundational step toward a unified central administration in British India.

answerOptions.text: The presidencies were merged into a single administrative unit governed directly from Calcutta.
answerOptions.rationale: While they became subordinate, they remained distinct administrative presidencies with their own Governors.

answerOptions.text: The Governors of these presidencies were appointed members of the Governor-General’s Executive Council.
answerOptions.rationale: The act established a separate council for the Governor-General of Bengal, but did not automatically include the other Governors.

questions.hint: Consider the initial steps taken by the British to create a centralized hierarchy among the different company-held regions.

questions.question: The Pitt's India Act of $1784$ is noted for establishing a 'Dual System of Governance.' Which body was specifically tasked with overseeing political, military, and revenue affairs?

answerOptions.text: Court of Directors
answerOptions.rationale: Under the dual system, this body was restricted to managing only the commercial affairs of the Company.

answerOptions.text: Secretary of State for India
answerOptions.rationale: This office was not created until the Government of India Act of $1858$, following the $1857$ revolt.

answerOptions.text: Board of Control
answerOptions.rationale: This body allowed the British government to exert supreme control over the Company's civil, military, and revenue operations.

answerOptions.text: Viceroy’s Executive Council
answerOptions.rationale: The title of Viceroy and the specific structure of his council are features of the later Crown Rule era.

questions.hint: Distinguish between the body representing the Company's shareholders and the body representing the British government's interests.

questions.question: Which of the following describes the status of the East India Company's trade monopoly following the Charter Act of $1813$?

answerOptions.text: It was completely abolished for all commodities and regions.
answerOptions.rationale: The act maintained specific commercial protections for the company regarding certain goods and locations.

answerOptions.text: It was extended for another twenty years without any modifications.
answerOptions.rationale: While the company rule was extended, its commercial monopoly was significantly curtailed to allow other British merchants in.

answerOptions.text: It ended for general trade in India but was preserved for tea and trade with China.
answerOptions.rationale: These two exceptions remained the last vestiges of the company's exclusive commercial rights in the East.

answerOptions.text: It was restricted solely to the trade of opium and salt within the Bengal presidency.
answerOptions.rationale: The specific exceptions defined in the act were tea and the geographically specific trade with China.

questions.hint: Recall the two major exceptions that allowed the Company to retain a partial commercial advantage until $1833$.

questions.question: The Charter Act of $1833$ is considered the final step towards centralization in British India. How did it alter the legislative authority of the Governors of Bombay and Madras?

answerOptions.text: It empowered them to create regulations that could only be vetoed by the British Parliament.
answerOptions.rationale: The act actually stripped them of legislative independence rather than granting them more autonomy.

answerOptions.text: It deprived them of their legislative powers, vesting exclusive authority in the Governor-General of India.
answerOptions.rationale: This centralized all law-making power for the entire British Indian territory into a single office.

answerOptions.text: It required them to submit all proposed laws to the Supreme Court at Calcutta for judicial review.
answerOptions.rationale: Legislative power was shifted to the executive Governor-General, not the judiciary.

answerOptions.text: It granted them the power to legislate on local matters while the Governor-General handled 'Federal' matters.
answerOptions.rationale: A division of subjects between center and provinces did not emerge until much later council and government acts.

questions.hint: Focus on the shift in power that occurred when the Governor-General of Bengal became the Governor-General of India.

questions.question: Regarding the Charter Act of $1853$, which innovation was introduced to the legislative process for the first time?

answerOptions.text: The inclusion of local representatives from provincial governments in the Central Legislative Council.
answerOptions.rationale: The act added six new members, four of whom were from the provincial governments of Madras, Bombay, Bengal, and Agra.

answerOptions.text: The establishment of a separate electorate for religious minorities to ensure representation.
answerOptions.rationale: Communal representation through separate electorates was not introduced until the Morley-Minto reforms of $1909$.

answerOptions.text: The creation of a 'Portfolio System' where each member of the council was in charge of a specific department.
answerOptions.rationale: The portfolio system was introduced by Lord Canning in $1859$ and recognized by the Act of $1861$.

answerOptions.text: The right of the council to discuss the budget and move resolutions on financial matters.
answerOptions.rationale: These deliberative functions were expanded later in the Acts of $1892$ and $1909$.

questions.hint: Look for the earliest instance of local provincial involvement in the 'Mini Parliament' at the center.

questions.question: The Government of India Act of $1858$ created the office of the Secretary of State for India. What was the primary nature of the $15$-member council established to assist this office?

answerOptions.text: It was a sovereign legislative body capable of overriding the British Parliament on Indian matters.
answerOptions.rationale: The Secretary of State was directly responsible to the British Parliament, which remained the ultimate authority.

answerOptions.text: It was an advisory body chaired by the Secretary of State.
answerOptions.rationale: This council provided expertise and assistance, but the Secretary of State held the primary executive authority.

answerOptions.text: It was a judicial panel intended to serve as the highest court of appeal for Indian civil cases.
answerOptions.rationale: The Council of India was an administrative and advisory organ, not a court of law.

answerOptions.text: It was a democratically elected body representing the various princely states.
answerOptions.rationale: Members of this council were appointed, and representation of princely states in central bodies was not a feature of the $1858$ Act.

questions.hint: Consider the role of the council in relation to the Secretary of State, who was a member of the British Cabinet.

questions.question: The Indian Councils Act of $1861$ is described as a 'Landmark' for several reasons. Which provision of this act signaled the beginning of decentralization?

answerOptions.text: The abolition of the office of the Secretary of State for India.
answerOptions.rationale: This office remained central to Indian administration until $1947$.

answerOptions.text: The restoration of legislative powers to the Bombay and Madras Presidencies.
answerOptions.rationale: This reversed the centralizing trend of $1833$ and eventually led to internal autonomy for provinces.

answerOptions.text: The introduction of direct elections for all members of the provincial councils.
answerOptions.rationale: Direct elections were first introduced by the Government of India Act of $1919$.

answerOptions.text: The requirement that all executive decisions be approved by a majority of Indian members.
answerOptions.rationale: While Indians were included as non-official members, they did not have the power to block executive decisions.

questions.hint: Think about how this act reversed the legal restrictions placed on the subordinate presidencies in $1833$.

questions.question: Which reform, introduced by the Government of India Act of $1919$, established a dual system of administration at the provincial level?

answerOptions.text: Bicameralism
answerOptions.rationale: This refers to a two-house legislature, which was introduced at the center in $1919$, not the dual administrative system in provinces.

answerOptions.text: Dyarchy
answerOptions.rationale: This system divided provincial subjects into 'Transferred' and 'Reserved' categories, though it was eventually deemed a failure.

answerOptions.text: Provincial Autonomy
answerOptions.rationale: Provincial autonomy was a feature of the $1935$ Act, which actually abolished the provincial dyarchy system.

answerOptions.text: Portfolio System
answerOptions.rationale: This system relates to the internal organization of the executive council and was recognized much earlier in $1861$.

questions.hint: This term comes from a Greek word meaning 'double rule' and refers to the splitting of subjects between the Governor and his ministers.

questions.question: Under the Government of India Act of $1935$, where were the 'Residuary Powers' (powers not specifically allocated to the federal, provincial, or concurrent lists) vested?

answerOptions.text: The Federal Legislature
answerOptions.rationale: In the $1935$ framework, the legislature did not hold the default authority for unlisted subjects.

answerOptions.text: The Provincial Governors
answerOptions.rationale: While provinces gained autonomy, the specific grant of residuary authority remained at the center with the crown representative.

answerOptions.text: The Governor-General
answerOptions.rationale: This followed a centralized logic where the head of the federation held any authority not specifically delegated elsewhere.

answerOptions.text: The Secretary of State for India
answerOptions.rationale: This office held administrative control from London but was not the designated repository for residuary legislative power within the Indian federation.

questions.hint: Identify the highest executive authority in India under the $1935$ federal scheme.

questions.question: Following the Indian Independence Act of $1947$, the Constituent Assembly performed dual roles. Who chaired the assembly when it functioned specifically as a legislative body (Dominion Legislature)?

answerOptions.text: Dr. Rajendra Prasad
answerOptions.rationale: He chaired the assembly when it functioned in its constituent capacity to frame the constitution.

answerOptions.text: G.V. Mavlankar
answerOptions.rationale: He presided over the sessions when the assembly acted as the Parliament for the dominion.

answerOptions.text: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar
answerOptions.rationale: He was the chairman of the Drafting Committee, which was responsible for writing the text of the constitution.

answerOptions.text: Satyendra Prasad Sinha
answerOptions.rationale: He is notable for being the first Indian to join the Viceroy's executive council in $1909$, not for chairing the assembly.

questions.hint: Differentiate between the person presiding over constitution-making and the person presiding over ordinary legislative business.
